assignments.description: Terminal fault sink. This flow runs after save on the record being activated, so an unhandled fault would roll back the activation itself — blocking a user from activating a contract because a decision table could not be refreshed, which is far worse than the stale table this flow exists to prevent. Capturing the message here ends the flow quietly instead. Nothing durable is written: this variable is not persisted, and the fault case that produces it — an invalid or inactive table API name — resolves to no table record, so it leaves no trace on DecisionTable either. Detect it by comparing each table's LastSyncDate against its own source, which is the only check that holds for every failure shape; see the Runtime-created pricing rows section of the pricing-wiring skill.
assignments.name: Absorb_Refresh_Fault
assignments.label: Absorb Refresh Fault

Flow.description: Refreshes the three contract pricing decision tables when a contract becomes Activated, so its contract prices are visible to pricing. Those tables are otherwise only built at org build time, and a contract sold afterwards is silently invisible to pricing — its negotiated price never applies, with no error. Triggered on ACTIVATION rather than creation because Contract_Pricing_Adjustment_Tiers and Contract_Pricing_Volume_Tiers both filter their source on ContractItemPriceId.ContractId.StatusCode = Activated: refreshing while the contract is still Draft excludes its rows and stamps LastSyncDate anyway, which reads as fresh while holding nothing. The entry condition matches on StatusCode, not Status, for the same reason — Status is a customizable picklist whose values map onto a StatusCode, so an org that activates into a custom value such as Signed would satisfy the tables' criteria while never matching a literal Status of Activated. To tell whether a refresh actually happened, compare each table's LastSyncDate against its own source: it only advances on a refresh that ran, so it is the one signal that holds for every failure shape. RefreshStatus / RefreshFailureReason only report an accepted refresh for a table that exists, and say nothing about an invocation fault.
Flow.interviewLabel: RLM Contract Activation Refresh Pricing Tables {!$Flow.CurrentDateTime}
Flow.label: RLM Contract Activation Refresh Pricing Tables

variables.description: Holds the fault message from a refresh that threw, so the fault is handled and the contract activation is not rolled back. Deliberately not an output and not persisted — it exists only to give the fault somewhere to land. To find out that a refresh did not happen, compare each table's LastSyncDate against its own source rather than looking for a record of the failure.
variables.name: refreshFaultMessage
